target_intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
comment: Same pick as my rank 2, so take this as agreement with one objection: your notes promise a round-2 veto for any intensive rank-1 that starts without organ-function labs, but the labs are a day's work while her peripheral blasts went 58 to 82% inside a few weeks, and delay is the one toxicity nobody on this board has tabulated. The Giles floor gets used asymmetrically too: if 58% (pmid:18076637) is not her number because that cohort lacks her hard features, then 13% (pmid:15973664) is not her number either, since Giles credits a long first remission and hers ran six years. Draw the creatinine and the echo on day 0 and start; a veto without a clock on it puts delay at rank 1.

target_intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
comment: You charge the conditioning platform a cost your rank 1 pays identically: 'no CR figure will ever attach to it' is just as true of NCT04050280, which has published nothing in refractory AML, so both picks stand on eligibility plus a borrowed backbone number. Critic's criterion-4 result shrinks that cost further, since every matched true-CR interval overlaps every other and the numbers that do attach cannot tell the options apart. Your own ASAP citation (pmid:38583455) prices the remission she would buy first at 61% versus 21% grade 3+ non-haematological toxicity and 27 extra hospital days for a day-56 CR of 79% against 83%, which argues the FLAMSA-type platform up your list, not down.

target_intervention_label: CPX-351 (liposomal daunorubicin/cytarabine) plus venetoclax (NCT03629171)
comment: Criterion 4 lands hardest on your own rank 1: the Wilson interval on 5/33 true CR runs 6.7 to 30.9 (pmid:40401707) and contains the Giles floor (pmid:15973664) and every alternative, so the most transferable number in the file is precise about a result nobody wants, priced at 21% dead by day 60 plus re-exposure to a drug she progressed through weeks ago. Two findings since round 1 make it worse: Vyxeos is labelled for newly diagnosed t-AML/AML-MRC only, and under the ELN definition concensusite surfaced, a marrow-only response from a liposome with tissue-to-plasma ratios below 1 cannot be called a CR in a woman with a documented thigh sarcoma. On your criterion-2 objection to my rank 1, conceded: FLAMSA's 88% (pmid:16110027) does not transfer past a first allograft, but the concession kills the quotable number rather than the platform, because NCT04375631 admits her venetoclax-refractory state, NCT06928662's TBI puts the thigh in the field, and the procedural route is the one ranked option whose upside no matched interval has already bounded.

target_intervention_label: Fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin monotherapy
comment: The label buys supply, not a strategy: MyloFrance-1's 26% CR is first relapse, transplant-naive and venetoclax-naive (pmid:17051246), and single-agent Mylotarg against 85% marrow blasts is the on-label way to undertreat her, which is why my objection sits at your rank 2 while I co-sign your rank 1, where the same fractionated schedule rides inside CLAG-GO. Your ELN extramedullary finding is the best thing in this round and it strengthens the CD33 route rather than weakening it, because the paediatric PET/CT lesions (pmid:29734213) are now the only response evidence in the file that satisfies the question's own CR definition. The same access logic argues the lintuzumab-Ac225 expanded-access call from my round-1 notes onto the board's open-actions list rather than into the archive: 38.5% CR/CRi in prior-venetoclax patients (pmid:39955432) and in-vivo reversal of venetoclax resistance (pmid:33347715) are worth one letter to the sponsor before anyone settles under a 26% ceiling.

target_intervention_label: Sequential conditioning into a second allograft (CLAG-M or FLAG-Ida then RIC, NCT04375631; DEC-FLAG-Ida then TBI/RIC, NCT06928662)
comment: My pre-declared veto does not fire here: NCT04375631's entry gates force the creatinine clearance and DLCO documentation this case has never had before any conditioning drug goes in. The dissent is about the safety datum still missing after those gates clear, second-graft non-relapse mortality in active-disease post-allograft relapse, which neither platform has published; ASAP's 40-point grade 3+ toxicity advantage for skipping reinduction (61% vs 21%, 27 fewer hospital days, pmid:38583455) is the best argument for this route, and it was generated in first-allograft patients, so it does not transfer to her. FLAMSA's 88% (66/75, pmid:16110027) comes from mostly first transplants two decades before venetoclax, and with criterion 4 landed there is no demonstrated CR separation left to justify spending an unquantified procedural mortality on.

target_intervention_label: CPX-351 (liposomal daunorubicin/cytarabine) plus venetoclax (NCT03629171)
comment: This is the rank-1 my pre-declared threshold veto was aimed at, the one delivering an anthracycline into an unmeasured cardiac reserve, and I am withdrawing it rather than delivering it: NCT03629171 screens organ function at entry, so on protocol the labs arrive before the daunorubicin does, the same mitigation I credited to CLAG-GO. The dissent that remains rests on criterion 4: true CR 5/33 (Wilson 6.7-30.9, pmid:40401707) is indistinguishable from every alternative in a population containing her, so what distinguishes this pick now is its cost, and that cost is the worst documented on the board, 9% dead by day 30, 21% by day 60, six grade 5 events. The Vyxeos label covers newly diagnosed t-AML and AML-MRC only, so the most transferable number in the file buys a regimen that is off-indication in second salvage, no likelier to deliver the endpoint than its neighbours, and the most likely to kill her inside 60 days.

target_intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
comment: Same rank 1 as mine, so this is a condition rather than an objection: gemtuzumab's boxed hepatotoxicity and veno-occlusive disease warning travels with her into a possible second conditioning, and MyloFrance-1's clean record (no VOD, pmid:17051246) rests on seven transplanted patients, so hepatic labs before day 1 and re-adjudication of the GO component if they are abnormal belong inside the pick, not beside it. Advocate named the axis nobody measured, what treatment costs her in weeks of her life, and criterion 4 has now made it decisive: when every matched true-CR interval overlaps, cost is what separates the options, and that favours the one rank-1 with no anthracycline in it and a protocol-mandated organ screen (nct:NCT04050280). One further condition: ELN 2022 CR requires absence of extramedullary disease, so the protocol's marrow-based response assessment needs thigh imaging added, or the CR it declares will not be, for her, a CR.

target_intervention_label: Fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin monotherapy
comment: I am aiming at the rank-2 rather than the rank-1, which matches my own; the monotherapy is where we part. Label carriage is real, but the purchase is bad: single-agent GO gave 26% CR (15/57, pmid:17051246) in first-relapse patients who were transplant-naive and venetoclax-naive, so at roughly 85% marrow blasts her expected return sits well under a number that is already a ceiling, while the boxed hepatotoxicity/VOD warning costs the same whether the drug works or not, and a prior allograft with a possible second conditioning ahead is the exact setting that warning was written for. Fractionated GO inside CLAG-GO spends that hepatic risk on a cladribine backbone's chance at the endpoint; spent on monotherapy at her burden, the same risk buys the weakest expected benefit on this board.

target_intervention_label: Sequential conditioning into a second allograft (CLAG-M or FLAG-Ida then RIC, NCT04375631; DEC-FLAG-Ida then TBI/RIC, NCT06928662)
comment: I put this platform at rank 2 myself, and the strongest case for it is the one risktaker did not make: ASAP (pmid:38583455) prices the buy-a-remission-first route at 61% versus 21% grade 3+ non-haematological toxicity and a median 27 extra hospital days for a day-56 CR difference of 3.4%, which is a patient-side cost argument, whereas taking 'an 88% with a flawed denominator over a well-matched 13%' is an appetite argument, and the appetite is risktaker's rather than hers; an empty toxicity_vetoes array records that nobody asked, not that she answered. The cost this platform actually carries, second-graft non-relapse mortality at roughly 85% blasts, has no published figure on either open protocol (nct:NCT04375631, nct:NCT06928662), so consenting her honestly means saying out loud that the number does not exist. And the expanded-access call to the lintuzumab-Ac225 sponsor (pmid:39955432) that risktaker's own notes asked for has still not been made; it is one phone call, it was hers to have had made on her behalf, and if the answer is yes both our rankings change.

target_intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
comment: Same rank 1 for the same reason, and the pre-declared threshold veto is the right way to hold an empty veto list: conservative refuses to read her silence as consent, which is exactly what preferences.json::free_text asked for when it said the 0.75 efficacy weight 'should be revisited once fitness is known', and fitness is still not known. The gemtuzumab handling should reach the PI verbatim, no VOD in seven transplanted patients on MyloFrance-1 being reassurance from a denominator of seven rather than proof (pmid:17051246), because she may be headed to a second graft and most of this board, me included, ranked a gemtuzumab-containing pick without anyone putting that trade to her. One push: conservative's notes name the gap that matters most, that nobody has offered her a 13 to 17% chance of the intended result (pmid:15973664) against a 7 to 21% chance of dying inside 60 days and asked whether she wants it, and that conversation is an action item for her team before day 1, not a caveat in this file.

target_intervention_label: CPX-351 (liposomal daunorubicin/cytarabine) plus venetoclax (NCT03629171)
comment: Criterion 4 landed, and it indicts my ordering along with everyone else's: when every true-CR interval containing her overlaps every other, no list under a heading that promises 'most likely to induce a complete remission' is honestly ordered by that promise. Critic's fix, relabelling the order as evidence quality and population match, does not dissolve the consequence: once the candidates tie on the intended benefit, what separates them is what each one costs her, and this rank 1 is the most expensive deliverable option on the page, 21% dead by day 60 for a 15% true CR that is marrow-only and therefore not an ELN CR for a woman with a thigh sarcoma (pmid:40401707), against 3.6% 30-day mortality in the closest post-allograft cohort (pmid:42499388). The most transferable number is an epistemic virtue, not a patient benefit, and ordering by it puts the worst documented early mortality at the top of a page she will read as 'what to do', on a cost axis nobody has asked her about.

target_intervention_label: Fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin monotherapy
comment: Taking the rank 2 because their rank 1 is also mine. Two findings here are genuinely hers: on-label supply means she could simply be given this, no trial slot, no screening gate, no appeal, a real difference from every other candidate in the file; and the ELN 2022 point that CR requires absence of extramedullary disease (pmid:35797463) is the most patient-protective sentence on this board, since it turns every marrow-only figure in the dossier into a labelled partial answer instead of a false promise about her thigh, and this happens to be the only agent where anyone imaged an extramedullary lesion at response (pmid:29734213), even if that was two children. Qualified all the same: 26% true CR (pmid:17051246) comes from first-relapse, transplant-naive, venetoclax-naive patients, a ceiling rather than her estimate, so rank 2 is an access argument wearing an efficacy rank, and the boxed VOD warning ahead of a possible second allograft is a trade her empty toxicity_vetoes array has never answered.

target_intervention_label: Sequential conditioning into a second allograft (CLAG-M or FLAG-Ida then RIC, NCT04375631; DEC-FLAG-Ida then TBI/RIC, NCT06928662)
comment: Criterion 2 was pre-registered to require remission data applicable after a prior allograft, and neither number here has it: FLAMSA's 88% (66/75, pmid:16110027) is mostly first transplants two decades before venetoclax, and ASAP (pmid:38583455) enrolled patients heading to a first allograft with prior allo-HCT excluded, so 'an 88% with a flawed denominator' understates the problem; the denominator is the whole question. This list orders by headline magnitude and says so honestly, but on true CR in populations that actually contain her every interval overlaps every other (CPX-351-VEN 6.7-30.9, Byrne post-allo 11.8-48.8, MIRROS control 11.4-24.7, Giles second salvage 10.3-15.7), so no ranking this round is ordering by demonstrated CR probability, and a rank 1 drawn from a population she was excluded from, feeding protocols that will never publish a CR rate (nct:NCT04375631, nct:NCT06928662), sits furthest of the five from the endpoint as asked. The notes' pharmacology hit on my own rank 1 is fair and I take it: tissue:plasma below 1 for the liposome where free drug runs above 1 says the thigh needs its own plan, though that argues for adding radiotherapy to whichever regimen wins, and it cuts against every marrow-directed pick on this board, not just mine.

target_intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
comment: Calling this 'the best true-CR evidence among the regimens she can actually receive' borrows CLAG-M's number for a protocol with zero published results in refractory AML, and the borrowed footing is softer than quoted: the printed 58% (pmid:18076637) is 66/114 evaluable rather than the stated 66/118, which is 55.9%, a quotation error rather than a rank-changer but one that should stop travelling, and Price's 37.9% versus 23.8% at p=0.048 (pmid:21109304) is a single-centre retrospective with physician-assigned treatment and no adjustment, so it cannot carry a rank 1 either. What this list actually orders by is deliverability plus documented toxicity, which the conditional-on-organ-screen framing half admits; said outright it would be fine, because on true CR in populations containing her no interval separates from any other, which is criterion 4 landing on all five of us. The parts that hold are the organ-function threshold before day 1 and the refusal to quote 58% to her, though the closing line that every CR claim is a marrow claim now needs its stronger form: ELN 2022 CR requires absence of extramedullary disease (pmid:35797463), so a marrow-only response in a woman with a documented thigh sarcoma is not an ELN CR at all.

target_intervention_label: Fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin monotherapy
comment: Taking the rank 2 rather than the rank 1 because it carries the claim that needs pressure: the R/R CD33+ label is a regulatory fact whose evidentiary basis is MyloFrance-1 itself (pmid:17051246), a single-arm phase 2, n=57, first relapse only, transplant- and venetoclax-naive, no comparator, so 'label matches her line' adds nothing beyond the 26% CR (15/57) ceiling they already named, and this ranking orders by indication fit rather than CR evidence, which to their credit the rationale says. Both notes findings land on me and I concede them: Vyxeos labelled for newly diagnosed t-AML/AML-MRC only makes my rank 1 off-indication in second salvage, which changes nothing about what Kadia's 5/33 true CR in a 58%-prior-venetoclax, 30%-prior-transplant cohort (pmid:40401707) is worth as evidence, but it strips the off-protocol fallback, so that pick survives only as a slot on NCT03629171 and the synthesis should say so. Their ELN 2022 finding is stronger than they pressed it: with absence of extramedullary disease inside the definition, the file's marrow-only figures are not ELN CRs for her, and I re-score my criterion 5 from 'technically met, practically not' to unmet, because two paediatric PET-followed lesions with no CR grading (pmid:29734213) cannot support a marrow-plus-thigh remission claim for any candidate here.

target_intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
comment: Ranking the one protocol written to admit her is defensible, and this was the only round-1 position that said plainly what its ordering rests on, eligibility and backbone rather than a CR rate; criterion 4 forces that admission from everyone eventually, since on true CR in populations containing her every interval overlaps every other. The spread still needs repair: 13% through 26% to 58% hands her three numbers from three regimens and three populations as if they bracket her odds, and they do not, because Giles' stratification runs to 0% in its highest-risk group (pmid:15973664), so the honest floor sits below 13% even granting that her six-year first remission is a favourable factor on that model, while 26% (pmid:17051246) is first-relapse monotherapy, not a lower bound on this combination, and 58% (pmid:18076637) is 66/114 evaluable from a pre-venetoclax cohort with no post-allograft patients in it. And moderate confidence on rank-2 FLAMSA above low on their own rank 1 is inverted on this question's endpoint: both open platforms publish no remission endpoint at all (nct:NCT06928662, nct:NCT04375631) and ASAP excluded prior allograft (pmid:38583455), so nothing there can outrank a pick that at least has a number.

target_intervention_label: Sequential conditioning into a second allograft (CLAG-M or FLAG-Ida then RIC, NCT04375631; DEC-FLAG-Ida then TBI/RIC, NCT06928662)
comment: We are the two personas who questioned the goal instead of the options, and the PI should see that agreement plainly: ELN 2022 (pmid:35797463) manages post-transplant relapse through second HCT without writing a CR precondition into it, which is why this platform sits third on my own list. The rank is where I pull back, because ASAP (pmid:38583455) randomised patients heading to a first allograft, failed its non-inferiority test at the pre-specified 2.5% level, and no guideline has absorbed it (ELN 2022 predates it; the NCCN v3.2026 Insights, June 2026, pmid:42297017, are scoped to MRD), so rank 1 puts the platform ahead of both its evidence and its consensus. Credit where it is due on this question's own endpoint, though: the TBI platform is the one route on this board where her thigh sarcoma sits inside the treatment field by design, while every drug regimen would have to prove that coverage with imaging at response.

target_intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
comment: Her rank-1 is mine as well, and it stands on the strongest consensus footing available: NCCN has routed R/R AML to a clinical trial or R/R salvage since at least v3.2019 (pmid:31200351), no later version names a regimen for her line, and her organ-function condition rebuilds exactly the fit population the guideline text assumes. One sharpening of her notes, where she writes that any CR claim here is a marrow claim and should be written as one: ELN 2022 (pmid:35797463) puts absence of extramedullary disease inside the CR definition itself, so for a woman with a documented thigh sarcoma an unimaged marrow response is not an ELN CR however carefully it is worded. The fix costs one scan, and I would attach it to her conditions: repeat thigh MRI or PET/CT at first response assessment, written into the plan on protocol (nct:NCT04050280) or off.

target_intervention_label: CPX-351 (liposomal daunorubicin/cytarabine) plus venetoclax (NCT03629171)
comment: Carriage sinks this rank for me: Vyxeos is labelled for newly diagnosed t-AML and AML-MRC only (label effective 2026-01-30), NCCN's placement was always that frontline slot (v3.2019 carried it at category 2B for patients under 60, pmid:31200351), and no guideline anywhere lists CPX-351 plus venetoclax in second salvage, so rank 1 hands the write-up an off-indication, off-label regimen as the board's leading answer. That said, his criterion-4 finding and my round-1 position converge, and the convergence is the real result of this run: every matched Wilson interval overlaps (pmid:40401707 among them) while the guideline offers nothing but the trial route for her line, so the evidence position and the consensus position arrive at the same verdict, that no drug discriminates on demonstrated CR probability and the open protocol is the answer rather than the least-bad off-label regimen. His intervals also all rest on marrow-only endpoints, which under ELN 2022 (pmid:35797463) are not CRs for a patient with a thigh sarcoma, so even 'most transferable number in the file' claims more than the 15% actually measured.

target_intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
comment: Endorse on the pick, which needs no more argument from me than it got in my own row; this comment answers the question her notes leave open, whether any guideline measures what a treatment costs her in weeks of her life. There is language, but it lives next door to the AML texts: ASCO's 2024 guideline update on palliative care for patients with cancer (pmid:38748941) tells oncology clinicians to refer patients with advanced haematological malignancies to specialist palliative care early in the disease course, alongside active treatment, and that referral is the guideline instrument for putting hospital days and toxicity on the table as her outcomes rather than footnotes. ASAP (pmid:38583455) supplies the numbers to bring to that conversation: induction bought a 3.4% day-56 CR difference at the price of 61% versus 21% grade 3 or worse non-haematological adverse events and a median 27 extra hospital days, which is exactly the trade she has never been asked about.
